messages:
dmitri: quick heads-up: our backup-import job started failing at 04:12 UTC with KMS decrypt errors for wrapped audit blobs in gs://audit-backups/inference/. suspect this is related to the RBAC tidy that landed ~04:05.

rae: i removed stale grants from the keyring to tighten access earlier. did i accidentally remove the unwrap role from the importer SA?

carmen: which SA runs the import job? i can check iam.

secops-bot: Job failure alert: backup-importer-processor on redwood-infra reported 5 KMS_DECRYPT failures between 04:12-04:14 UTC. Logs: https://logs.internal/project/backup-importer/3612345678

kms-bot: current bindings for keyRing/secops: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter -> serviceAccount:wrap-n-unwrap@infra; roles/cloudkms.viewer -> group:infra-readers. No binding for serviceAccount:backup-importer@infra. Last change: RBAC-sweep-2026-03-29 applied by rae at 04:05 UTC.

dmitri: confirmed. backup-importer SA lost decrypt perms. that means we can't rehydrate plaintext audit events for the 'inference' namespace. we need a short-lived plan to recover events and then rotate any creds exposed in the missing window.

rae: proposal: i re-grant decrypt for 10 minutes, run import, then revoke. but prefer human unwrap to avoid adding perms back to SA. carmen, can you run a one-off gcloud decrypt under your dev account and place plaintext in a sealed evidence bucket?

carmen: i can. will need the wrapped object names and the key resource id. list?

dmitri: wrapped objects: gs://audit-backups/inference/2026-03-29-04-06.json.enc .. -04-15.json.enc (10 objects). key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/secops/cryptoKeys/evidence.

secops-bot: Note: policy for handling evidence requires: 1) copy wrapped blob to gs://secops-evidence/INC-2026-112/ 2) decrypt locally under approved account 3) compute sha256 and upload plaintext to sealed bucket with ACL secops-only.

carmen: doing copy now and prepping gcloud command.

kms-bot: request logged: Temporary decrypt grant would normally be requested via IAM-approvals workflow. emergency fast-track authorized by dmitri in-channel.

dmitri: fast-track ok. carmen, when you decrypt, grep for patterns: "VAULT_TOKEN", "service_key", "access_key_id", and IP addresses external-to-org. if you find anything, tag here immediately and we'll rotate.

carmen: decrypt output scan in progress. small snag: two blobs are truncated (04-09, 04-11), gcloud reports "unexpected EOF". saving partials to evidence.

vault-bot: scanning plaintext (automated): found one match in 04-08.json: pattern "VAULT_TOKEN=([A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,})". token appears to be for role 'batch-deploy' namespace 'inference'. last use recorded 04:07 UTC.

dmitri: treat as exposed. rotate now. who owns batch-deploy consumer? rae?

rae: i own rotation. plan: revoke token, create new short-lived token with minimal policy, update consumers, restart affected pods.

carmen: uploading decrypted blobs and SHA256s to gs://secops-evidence/INC-2026-112/. files: 2026-03-29-04-06.json.plain (sha256=a7f3...), 04-07.json.plain (sha256=8b1c...), partial_04-09.json.partial (sha256=ff12...). ACL set to secops-only.

secops-bot: Evidence stored and sealed. Access logged.

dmitri: rotation commands (rae):
```
vault token revoke -namespace=inference -token=REDACTED_OLD
vault token create -namespace=inference -policy=batch-minimal -ttl=1h -format=json | jq -r .auth.client_token
kubectl -n inference set secret generic batch-deploy-creds --from-literal=token=REDACTED_NEW
kubectl rollout restart deploy/batch-deploy -n inference
```

rae: executed. new token created and k8s secret updated. deploy restarted.

deploy-bot: rollout for batch-deploy started, status: in_progress.

vault-bot: old token revoked at 04:28 UTC. any child tokens also marked revoked.

dmitri: good. now import flow: either i temporarily grant decrypt to backup-importer for 8 minutes, run import, then revoke; or we keep human-decrypt path for chain-of-custody. preference: human decrypt for evidence, but allow importer to import the rest after we confirm no more creds leaked. rae, thoughts?

rae: do human decrypt for the 10 objects, import manually, then run a compare accounting: event counts from importer vs expected counts. if matches (minus truncated), revoke any temporary perms (if any) and close. also raise infra ticket to block RBAC sweep from removing keys used by operational pipelines.

dmitri: agreed. carmen, please post final counts and which blobs were truncated. then we can create incident INC-2026-112 with timeline and action owners.

carmen: final: decrypted 10 objects, 2 truncated partials (04-09, 04-11). importer dry-run shows 542 events available, 3 events rejected due to schema. plaintext scan found only the one VAULT_TOKEN, which is rotated. uploading final import report to incident doc.

secops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-112. Owners: dmitri, rae, carmen. Postmortem checklist added: add automated alert for KMS decrypt failures, require sink-owner acknowledgement before RBAC sweeps remove key bindings, periodic backup integrity check that validates blob sizes and checksums.

dmitri: done. closing here once the importer import is run and counts reconciled to 542. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
